title: Orbit Labs - Portability & Private Deploy Discovery
summary: Initial discovery to understand Orbit Labs' constraints for migrating from OpenAI-hosted prompts and a vLLM/TGI self-hosted stack into a more portable setup. Main concerns: eval parity, quantization/throughput, private VPC/on-prem options, SOC2 and KMS integration. Agreed to run parity benchmarks and share security/compliance pack.
topics: current stack: OpenAI + vLLM/TGI for internal infra
hosting choices: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
cost/latency tradeoffs, batching and KV cache
next steps: benchmarks, pricing, security docs
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + Private deployment checklist and KMS integration notes
Redwood SE to run initial eval parity benchmark with Orbit's prompt set (10k tokens sample)
Orbit to provide sample prompt set and representative latency SLOs by 2026-08-14
Schedule follow-up deep-dive (benchmark review) week of 2026-08-17
action_items: Maya Patel — Send SOC2, ISO docs + private deployment checklist (link) — due 2026-08-16
Ethan Cole — Build benchmark plan and run small vLLM->Redwood host parity test (use 10k token set) — due 2026-08-18
Rina Cho — Share prompt/trace sample and current token costs/usage patterns — due 2026-08-14
Priya Nambiar — Confirm regulatory constraints re: EU data residency and HSM requirement — due 2026-08-16
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Rina (Orbit HoML), Diego (Infra), Priya (Security), Tom (Product)
Link to deck: https://redwood.example/sales/deck-orbit (shared)

Summary: quick discovery to map migration surface area from their current OpenAI + vLLM/TGI stack into Redwood hosted/dedicated/private. Emphasis on eval parity and security.

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Can we do quick intros? we'll go 45-ish minutes and then leave time for q's.
[00:00:10] Rina: Hi I'm Rina, head of ML at Orbit, we run a hybrid setup, prod requests go to OpenAI historically, but last year we started self-hosting with v l l m and T G I for cost reasons.
[00:00:22] Diego: Diego here, infra eng, we manage the v v l m cluster and deployment.
[00:00:26] Priya: Priya, security lead. My immediate concerns are data residency and KMS/HSM integration.
[00:00:30] Tom: Tom, product. I'm mostly here to understand the impact on latency for user-facing features.
[00:00:35] Maya: Awesome. Quick overview: Redwood offers Hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private for VPC/on-prem. Today we want to see which path fits Orbit's constraints. Ethan will chime in on compatibility.
[00:00:50] Ethan: Hi all. Quick note: we've onboarded many vLLM and TGI-based customers; compatibility depends on model format, kv-cache handling and a few tokenizer quirks.
[00:01:05] Rina: Great. Our stack: control plane uses OpenAI API for some endpoints, but for cost we've shifted some traffic to our vLLM cluster running quantized models. We use sequence lengths around 1k tokens for most user flows, sometimes 2k.
[00:01:20] Diego: We run mixed A100 and T4 nodes, batching aggressively. We have a custom prefix cache but it's not uniformly applied.
[00:01:30] Maya: That helps. What are your current latency SLOs and 95th p99 targets?
[00:01:36] Tom: For core chat flows p95 is under 550ms; p99 we tolerate up to 1.2s. For background embeddings it's more throughput-oriented.
[00:01:48] Maya: Good to know. Cost targets?
[00:01:51] Rina: We're roughly at $0.003 per token equivalent with heavy batching, but OpenAI costs are spiking on some features. We're trying to get unit cost down without sacrificing eval parity.
[00:02:03] Priya: On security: we need SOC2 type II, SSO with SAML + SCIM for provisioning, audit logs exported to our SIEM, and optional HSM for key ops. Also EU data residency for certain customers.
[00:02:18] Maya: Totally standard. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and can operate in VPC with private control plane. We also support audit exports via syslog or S3 with encryption.
[00:02:30] Priya: And can you integrate with existing HSMs? We use a YubiHSM at the moment.
[00:02:34] Ethan: We have done HSM/KMS integrations for a handful of customers; typically we integrate with AWS KMS and on-prem HSMs through KMIP or a gateway. We'll detail options in the security pack.
[00:02:48] Rina: On compatibility: our prompts include some instruction-following tests and reranking. We're worried about tiny differences in tokenization and quantization artifacts affecting quality.
[00:02:59] Ethan: Right. Two areas to watch: tokenizer differences (we've seen slight subtoken mapping) and quantization model artifacts. We usually run eval parity on a 1k prompt set and compare rouge/bleu or direct output match rates.
[00:03:15] Diego: For throughput, our key technique is large batch aggregation and prefix caching — we call it prefix cache but it's basically a KV cache of prefix embeddings. How does Redwood handle that?
[00:03:25] Maya: Redwood runtime includes automatic KV cache reuse and prefix caching heuristics. For Dedicated we can expose more aggressive batching windows; for Hosted there are tighter latency SLOs but still good caching.
[00:03:36] Diego: Are the caching semantics compatible with vLLM's approach? We need deterministic cache keys since we share cache across replicas.
[00:03:43] Ethan: We support deterministic KV keys and can map your existing key schema. There may be differences in eviction policy, but we can align. We'll include a mapping document.
[00:03:55] Tom: Can you explain fallback policies? If Dedicated capacity is saturated do you have fallbacks to hosted variants?
[00:04:02] Maya: Yes. Smart routing can fallback to other compatible model variants in the same region or different capacity tiers. That's configurable per-route.
[00:04:10] Rina: Ok, about model formats — we use GGUF and some ONNX exports for certain models. We also run Mistral-style weights and some community LLMs.
[00:04:20] Ethan: GGUF and standard PyTorch/transformers formats are supported. For ONNX we may need to check operator coverage. If you can share a model sample we'll run a quick import check.
[00:04:30] Priya: What about telemetry and tracing? We need per-request traces for audit.
[00:04:35] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-request trace IDs, and hooks to push traces to OpenTelemetry collectors.
[00:04:45] Diego: How does the billing work for Dedicated vs Private? We need predictable committed spend for infra budgeting.
[00:04:51] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits and burst options. Private is typically an enterprise license with support and on-prem costs. Hosted is pay-as-you-go. We can show cost modeling once we have your throughput numbers.
[00:05:02] Tom: On eval parity: if we migrate from OpenAI to Redwood Hosted, what's the usual delta? Any surprises?
[00:05:09] Ethan: It depends on the model variant. If you're already running open models on vLLM, parity can be very close. Differences usually surface with quantized weights and attention kernels; we provide quantization profiles and can recommend a profile that minimizes regression.
[00:05:24] Rina: Do you have automated regression alerts tied to prompt sets?
[00:05:28] Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring against prompt sets and will send regression alerts. You can tie thresholds to rollbacks.
[00:05:36] Priya: For compliance: are logs immutable? We need tamper-evident storage.
[00:05:40] Ethan: We support WORM-style S3 exports and append-only logs for audit trails. We'll include specifics.
[00:05:47] Diego: Curious about model rollout and canarying — can we do A/B test between vLLM host and Redwood endpoint?
[00:05:54] Maya: Absolutely. You can route x% to Redwood, measure quality and latency, and either ramp or rollback. Can do header-based routing too.
[00:06:02] Tom: For private deployments, how much ops commitment is required from our side?
[00:06:06] Maya: Private can be fully managed with a customer-controlled network, or we can provide an on-prem package where your infra team runs it and we provide updates. Ops involvement depends on the model of deployment you pick.
[00:06:16] Rina: Let's talk technical deep-dive items we'll need from you to run parity: tokenizer mapping, quantization profile, inference kernel differences, decoding settings, and a benchmark plan.
[00:06:27] Ethan: Noted. Our parity checklist will include tokenization diff, sample outputs, metric comparisons, and performance counters (p95/p99, tokens/sec). We'll need your sample prompts and a few golden outputs.
[00:06:39] Priya: For KMS, we need proof of key ownership flow — that customer keys never leave our HSM. Is that possible?
[00:06:45] Ethan: With Private and customer-managed KMS, we can ensure key material remains in your HSM and we call it via a gateway. We'll include cryptographic attestation docs.
[00:06:55] Rina: On quantization: we've seen LLMs differ when moving from 16-bit to 4-bit QAT or static quantization. Can you reproduce our exact quantization recipe?
[00:07:05] Ethan: We have quantization profiles and sometimes need to retrain or do calibration using your dataset. For many customers, activations and symmetric quant work, but we'll run calibration tests.
[00:07:18] Diego: Networking: how's egress handled for private? We have strict firewall rules.
[00:07:22] Maya: Private supports private endpoints, no public internet egress from inference plane unless you opt-in. Control plane comms can be over peered VPC or dedicated link.
[00:07:33] Tom: Any customers in EU doing private deployments with residency?
[00:07:36] Maya: Yes, several. We'll redact names but include patterns in the security pack.
[00:07:41] Rina: On the benchmarking — we want to test 1) output parity (accuracy metrics) 2) latency under p95/p99 3) cost per token with batching.
[00:07:50] Ethan: We'll design an experiment: run your 1k prompt samples on your vLLM->current and on Redwood Dedicated/Hosted as needed, collect tokens/sec and per-token cost. We'll also check decoding determinism.
[00:08:05] Priya: Is Redwood able to sign BAA? We occasionally handle PHI and need HIPAA considerations.
[00:08:11] Maya: We have enterprise contracts that can include BAA; we'll flag legal for specifics.
[00:08:17] Tom: How long does a pilot usually take?
[00:08:20] Maya: Typical pilot for parity and small production readiness is 2–6 weeks depending on dataset and model variety.
[00:08:26] Rina: That sounds reasonable. If we decide to do Dedicated vs Private, what's the provisioning lead time?
[00:08:31] Maya: Dedicated pools usually provision within 1–2 weeks after contract; Private depends on network/ops but often 4–8 weeks for on-prem with customer approvals.
[00:08:42] Diego: If we keep our vLLM cluster for some traffic, can Redwood routing split by model or route, like partial migration?
[00:08:48] Ethan: Yes. You can route per-route and per-model. That was customers' typical lift-and-shift strategy.
[00:08:54] Rina: Any gotchas with token counting differences between OpenAI and local vLLM exports?
[00:08:58] Ethan: Tokenization differences can change cost accounting; we usually provide a token equivalence mapping and tooling to re-count. For billing we apply our tokenization rules but will show reconciliation examples.
[00:09:12] Tom: Are there built-in tools to warm caches across restarts? We have ephemeral nodes.
[00:09:16] Maya: The runtime supports persisted KV cache to networked storage and fast recovery; with Dedicated you can enable sticky caching and pre-warm.
[00:09:26] Diego: For the benchmark, can we use our private dataset? We'd prefer to not share production data.
[00:09:31] Ethan: We can run the benchmark inside a Private deployment or you can pseudonymize and share. We also support client-executed benchmarks with Redwood agents to avoid data transfer.
[00:09:42] Rina: Great. Let's talk pricing — ballpark numbers for Dedicated reserved GPU pools and expected token costs compared to OpenAI?
[00:09:50] Maya: Ballpark only: Hosted is generally lower than OpenAI for inference-heavy open models; Dedicated depends on commit size. We'll produce a cost model after we see tokens/sec.
[00:09:59] Priya: Legal — we'll need standard DPAs and to know about subcontractors.
[00:10:03] Maya: We'll include DPA and SOC2 attestation and a subcontractor list.
[00:10:08] Rina: Anything else we should include in the parity plan?
[00:10:11] Ethan: We'll add tolerances (exact match thresholds), failure cases, and a rollback plan. Also, we should specify seed randomness and sampling settings to make comparisons fair.
[00:10:22] Tom: On sampling, we currently use top_p 0.9 and temperature 0.7 for most user flows.
[00:10:27] Ethan: We'll align those settings during parity runs.
[00:10:30] Maya: Next steps recap: Maya sends security and private deployment docs; Ethan builds bench plan; Orbit to send sample prompts and their throughput numbers. Follow-up week of Aug 17.
[00:10:40] Rina: Sounds good. One thing — we run a reranker pipeline that expects deterministic logits for scoring. Can Redwood provide logits in the response?
[00:10:48] Ethan: Yes, we can return logits and per-token probabilities if you enable structured output. We support logit APIs.
[00:10:56] Diego: Great. Also, how do you handle model updates/versioning during canary? We need predictable model pinning.
[00:11:02] Maya: You can pin model versions and create canary rollouts with automatic fallback. We keep model lineage in the Console.
[00:11:10] Tom: Any references or case studies for similar migrations?
[00:11:13] Maya: We'll share a couple of anonymized case studies and a benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:11:17] Priya: Please include the HSM integration case study if possible.
[00:11:20] Maya: Will do.
[00:11:22] Rina: Ok that's all from me, thanks.
[00:11:25] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll send docs and schedule the benchmark deep-dive.
[00:11:30] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (v l l m for vLLM, T G I for TGI) and some names spelled inconsistently. Links: benchmark sheet (https://redwood.example/benchmarks/orbitlab-sample), security pack (https://redwood.example/security/orbit)
